title: pokeheartgold
brief: A full decompilation of Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver — everything in C/C++, both ROMs building byte-for-byte, assembled with LLM agents; the tweeter notes about a month of work and roughly $56k at API prices for 4.1MB of compiled code. A remarkable reverse-engineering reference for ROM hackers and a real-world case study of agent-driven decompilation at scale. - Warning: the cost/time figures are from the announcement tweet; the repo is a fork — pret (upstream) doesn't accept AI-generated code and asks that nothing be sent upstream.
details: A full decompilation of Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver by ctrl-cheeb-del: the entire game in C/C++, with both ROMs (pokeheartgold.us.nds and pokesoulsilver.us.nds) building byte-for-byte from source. It is a fork of pret's pokeheartgold project, assembled with LLM agents — the announcement notes roughly a month of agent work and about $56k in API costs to decompile 4.1MB of compiled code. The author warns that pret does not accept AI-generated code, so nothing should be sent upstream. Useful as a reverse-engineering reference for ROM hackers and as a large-scale case study of what coding agents can accomplish on decompilation tasks.
